title: 📡 U.S. prisons get official permission to jam smuggled phones!
body: 📡 U.S. prisons get official permission to jam smuggled phones!
The U.S. Federal Communications Commission has voted unanimously to allow local and state prisons to use jamming devices to stop smuggled mobile phones inside prisons.

Jamming devices were generally banned under communications law, except in some federal prisons. The new rule lets prisons apply for a license to operate licensed jamming devices, provided they pass strict technical standards and tests, ensure communications outside the prison walls are unaffected, and notify neighboring communities.

The commission's chairman said smuggled phones are used to arrange acts of violence and run drug and human-trafficking networks inside prisons, while the commission's only Democratic commissioner supported the decision while acknowledging possible risks to legitimate communications.
Simply put: a smuggled phone inside a prison is like a secret line connecting the prisoner to the outside world; jamming cuts that line, without touching the neighbors' phones outside the walls.
Do you support jamming phones inside prisons despite the risk to nearby communications?
